newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: EUTHANASIA ANNOUNCEMENT EXPECTED
A press conference will be held today at the home of the wife of Bob Dent, the first man to die under the Northern Territory's voluntary euthanasia law.
It's thought a woman will announce she is seeking to be the second person to utilise the law.
The press conference has been organised by pro-euthanasia doctor, Phillip Nitschke. No text received
The woman's expected to announce that she's seeking the required medical signatures which will enable her to begin the voluntary euthanasia process.
ONE DEAD AFTER STORM CAUSES HAVOC
Emergency Service workers have been working through the night at Singleton in the Upper Hunter Valley, after a wild storm hit the area late yesterday.
An 18-year-old man died when his car ran off a road and hit a tree, while several people were injured in the storm which has closed the local hospital.
Twenty patients were evacuated from Singleton hospital which will remain closed until early next week, while schools and the local police stations were also damaged.
The town may be declared a natural disaster area.
UNION WELCOMES INTERIM FEDERAL AWARD IN VICTORIA
The Community and Public Sector Union in Victoria has welcomed the Industrial Relations Commission's decision to announce an interim award for state public servants.
It's set to cost the Victorian Government nearly 50-million dollars.
More than 20,000 public servants will receive three year's worth of accumulated leave loading, while about 11,000 will get a retrospective pay rise of between 7 and 10 per cent.
Karen Batt, of the Community and Public Sector Union, says it's one of the most important decisions handed down by the I-R-C.
The IRC's recommendations end a four year battle, with the interim award taking effect immediately, and workers getting pay rises next week.
FARMER BEGINS ULTRA-RUN TODAY
Australian ultra-distance runner Pat Farmer today begins his attempt to break the record for running run across the Simpson Desert.
Farmer plans to run from Alka Seltzer Bore, in South Australia's far-north, to Birdsville, in south-west Queensland.
The record of three days 17 hours and 52 minutes for the 379-kilometre run, was set 10 years ago, by Ron Grant of Queensland.
Temperatures may reach 60-degrees on some sections of the run, but Farmer says he's taken every possible safety precaution.
MTTA NOT CONVINCED ABOUT CHEAPER PETROL
Australia's peak motor industry body has called on oil companies to help establish proper competition in the market place at the wholesale level.
The Motor Trades Association says it's not convinced consumers will derive any long-term price benefits from the Federal Government's petrol industry reform package.
The MTTA's John Buckby has welcomed some aspects of the package, including the decision to abandon maximum wholesale price fixing for petrol next year.
But Mr Bucky says until all petrol retailers can get equal access to the best available wholesale price, there won't be an across the board cut in prices.
BABY DRAGONS BIRTH EAGERLY AWAITED
Researchers from around the world are eagerly awaiting the birth of 22 baby Komodo Dragons, bred for the first time in captivity in Australia.
The eggs from one of six dragons, gifts from Indonesian President Suharto to the Wyndham Crocodile Farm as part of an exchange, have been placed in an incubator and will take about 8 months to hatch.
Farm Owner, Don Weiringa says while zoos around the world have failed to breed the animals, Wyndham so far has been successful.
Mr Wieringa says Arnold, a two metre male dragon, is so happy in his new surrounds, he's mated again.
And Arnold may soon have another playmate.
Later this month, Serena, a four metre Komodo from Sydney's Taronga Zoo, will join the breeding programme.
MELBOURNE TO DARWIN INLAND RAIL LINK MOOTED
The feasibility of an inland rail link between Melbourne and Darwin is to by investigated.
The proposed six-billion dollar project would provide an inland freight and passenger route with links to major ports.

The Australian Trunk Rail Corporation, a private company, has been set up to look at the viability of the link, which would pass through Victoria, New South Wales, Queensland and the Northern Territory.
The company is hoping the Federal Government will make a contribution to the five-million dollar feasibility study.
TASSIE LOOKS FORWARD TO COTTON/WOOL BOOM
Tasmanian Premier, Tony Rundle, says a wool/cotton blend fabric conceived and developed in Tasmania has the potential to value-add the state's world-class rural and fashion industries.
The product is said to be the fabric of the next century and could replace denim in the manafacturing of jeans.
The fabric is a blend of 70 per cent Australian cotton and 30 per cent fine merino wool.
Mr Rundle says the fabric, to be grown, spun, woven and dyed in Tasmania and weaved in Launceston has great interstate and overseas export potential.
TELSTRA SALE COULD RAISE MORE THAN EXPECTED
Independent Senators, Mal Colston and Brian Harradine, have kept their word and supported legislation allowing the sale of one-third of Telstra to pass in the Senate.
The partial sale was finally approved last night, and investors should be able to buy into the company within the next 18 months.
But the Government did suffer one set back, the Senate voting for the retention of Ministerial control over the Telstra Board after the sale.
Communications Minister, Richard Alston, says this could affect the sale price, which the Government estimates at eight-billion dollars, part of which will be spent on environmental projects.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
